Commentary.Commentary: 106 to win. Is this going to be a bowlers' night? Australia showed plenty of nerves on the field. England showed plenty of nerves with the bat. Will the roles be reversed in the second innings? The run chase is just around the corner.

Credit has to go to Australia's bowlers. It would have been so easy to break down seeing so many chances fluffed. But they hung in. Kept bowling on good areas and reaped rewards. Ashleigh Gardner was the pick of the bowlers, with 3/22, which included the wickets of Wyatt and Knight. Wareham and Schutt grabbed 2 each and were economical as well.
Just two players could manage double figures. The pitch is on the slower side but England could not quite rotate the strike enough.

The game started with Danielle Wyatt taking the bull by the horns and the pressure of the final started to show on Australia. They kept dropping catch after catch but so good was their bowling, that England could not quite capitalize. The turning point came in the 11th over, when England were 64/3. Wyatt was dismissed and from there on, it was just a slide.
Wow. 6 dropped catches. One catch not reviewed. 2 run outs missed. That is a total of 9 opportunities let go by. Yet, Australia have bowled England out for 105. Hats off to the bowlers.
OUT! LBW! AUSTRALIA NEED 106 TO WIN THEIR FOURTH WWT20 TITLE. Full and straight, Hazell plays all around it, looking to flick and is hit right in front of the stumps. Easy decision for the umpire.
Chips this towards mid on for a single to get off the mark on her very first ball.
Kirstie Gordon is the last batter in. Never batted for England before.

OUT! Easy run out. Ecclestone worked it through mid-wicket and decided to chance Ellyse Perry's arm. The fielder smartly threw it on the bounce and the jog from Sophie could not quite get her home as Healy whipped off the bails.
Is that a run out? Referred upstairs...
Full and down the leg side, Hazell swipes hard and gets it off the inner half through square leg for a single.
Change of ball and bowler. It is getting increasingly dewy and the umpires agree to get the ball changed, owing to the wetness. Megan Schutt to bowl the final over. 3-0-10-1 so far.

A high full toss, outside off, slapped over cover for a single. That should have been a no ball for waist but England do not get it. Harsh call and they are not happy. A single taken. 3-0-23-0 for Molineux tonight.

DROPPED AND A MISSED RUN OUT! Full and outside off, Ecclestone hits it aerially towards the bowler who sticks out her left hand and parries it to mid off instead. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Sophie was gone with a direct hit.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Comes down the track, hits it down the ground for a single. Hang on, long off misfields and long on overruns her. Converted into a double.
A stumping appeal, referred upstairs, but safe. Full and outside off, Ecclestone looked to defend but missed. Quick work from Healy behind which is shown up but replays show that Sophie is fine.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Sophie Ecclestone comes in at number 10, replacing Knight. Sophie Molineux returns as well. 2-0-19-0 so far.

OUT! Gone this time. Full and outside off, Knight comes down the track again, looking to go over the off side but the ball spins away and she miscues it. Simple catch for Georgia Wareham at mid off. 9 runs and a wicket from the over. Gardner finishes with figures of 4-0-22-3.

DROPPED, SIX! Fifth drop of the match by Australia. Full on middle, Knight comes down the track and looks to go downtown. Does not quite get hold of it and Beth Mooney at long on has a chance. She leaps but perhaps she has the thought of the fence behind. The ball brushes her fingertips and crosses the fence. Meg Lanning cannot believe it.
Easily done. Comes forward and pushes the ball to point for one.
Comes down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Landed outside off, Knight looks to play the reverse sweep but gets no pace to work with. Mistimes it to short third man.
Outside off, steered behind point for a single.
Outside off, a gentle tap and run to cover.
Short again, cut through point for one.
Dropped short, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler who fumbles but mid off backs her up.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, tapped through point for a single.
Megan Schutt is back into the attack. 2-0-6-1 so far.
Pushes this through mid on for a run.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Danielle Hazell walks in at number 9, replacing Shrubsole.
OUT! This time the catch is taken. Full and outside off, Shrubsole looks to slog but does not time it well. Easier catch for Ellyse Perry at deep mid-wicket. England are 7 down now.

SAFE. And England run on the deflection as well. Full and outside off, Knight drives it straight to mid off. Shrubsole wants a single but is sent back. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end and hits them and it is referred upstairs. Replays confirm that she is in. In the meanwhile, they have run off the deflection.
DIRECT HIT! Has Shrubsole made it back in time?

DROPPED! Oh dear... what happens when brilliance combines with the ordinary? A team is 83/6 when they should have been 70 all out. A short ball outside off, Shrubsole pulls it hard but straight to deep mid-wicket. Ellyse Perry in the deep is late to react as the ball dips on her. Puts it down. A single taken.
Full and outside off, Shrubsole looks to paddle but misses and is hit on her pads. An LBW appeal ensues but the impact is out side off.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Goes back and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
On middle and off, bunted back to the bowler.
Good running. Short and outside off, Anya cuts it through point and calls for two. It is tight but she makes it with a dive.
Floated around off, spinning away, Shrubsole looks to flick but gets a leading edge to mid off.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
WIDE. No hat-trick for Wareham. Full and down the leg side, Knight misses her paddle.
Hat-trick time!
Full and around off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, swept through fine leg for a run.
Another watchful defense from the batter.
Full and outside off, Shrubsole looks to defend but misses.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Full on middle, pushed through mid on for a single.
Anya Shrubsole walks in at number 8, replacing Dunkley. Ashleigh Gardner is back on too. 1-0-7-1 so far.

OUT! Two in two for Wareham! What a ball to the new batter. A yorker, fired in on leg stump, Dunkley is late in getting her bat down and the LED bails illuminate, as she gets bowled! What an over from the bowler.
Sophia Dunkley walks in at number 7, replacing Winfield.

OUT! LBW! Great review from Australia! They have their 5th wicket. Given they muffed so many chances, they could have had England all out by now. A touch short around off, the skidder, Winfield goes back to cut and on the first look, she gets it away to point. But Lanning, her bowler and keeper get together for a chat and signal for the review. One of them feels it is pad first. Sure enough, replays confirm that and Hawk Eye projects it to be in line and hitting the stumps!
A review from Australia for LBW now. Bat first or pad?

NOW, A STUMPING MISSED! Australia exploring all possible chances of mishaps in the field tonight. Floated around leg stump, Winfield comes down the track and looks to flick but misses. Alyssa Healy is blinded and the ball goes past her behind. Two byes taken.
Laps a full toss now, down the leg side again, for another brace.
Gets across her stumps and laps it from the line of the sticks through fine leg for a couple.
Down the leg side, flicked away for a single.
Georgia Wareham returns. 1-0-1-0 so far.
Outside off, driven straight to mid offf.

Outside off, Lauren looks to cut but misses. Healy starts to appeal but nothing from the bowler or the umpire. Lanning asks about the review but the bowler denies it. SNICKOMETER DETECTS A MASSIVE BOTTOM EDGE! Oh dear... Australia have missed another opportunity.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a couple.
Full and around off, defended back to the bowler.
Yorker outside off, Winfield cannot get it away.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Lauren Winfield walks in at number 6, replacing Wyatt. Delissa Kimmince is back on as well. 2-0-7-0 so far.

OUT! Stop the press. Australia have taken a catch. Wyatt departs, 7 short of a half century. Full and outside off, Wyatt hits it hard through the covers but Meg Lanning over there moves to her left, leaps and takes it around her midriff. Big wicket for Australia.
Comes down the track and heaves it to wide long on for one.
Down the leg side, swept straight to short fine leg.
Full and outside off, slogged down to long on for a run.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Another mishap in the field. Beth Mooney the culprit. Full and around middle, Wyatt comes down the track and looks to go aerial but mistimes it badly. The ball drops down to long on and Beth Mooney gets to her left but then slips and the ball goes through!
Down the leg side, helped through square leg for a single.
Ashleigh Gardner into the attack now.
Down the leg side, Knight misses her flick and the ball goes off her pads to short fine leg. A leg bye taken.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Goes for the cut but gets a bottom edge to short third man. A single taken.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Well outside off, Danielle gets across and looks to sweep again, to miss again. A mild LBW appeal ensues.
Full and down the leg side, Wyatt misses her flick and is hit on the pads.
Georgia Wareham into the attack now.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a run.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
Works it through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Rubbing salt on the wound. Outside off, Knight goes back and cuts it between short third man and backward point for a boundary! 50 UP FOR ENGLAND!

RUN OUT MISSED! Poor stuff from Alyssa Healy. Australia's fielding - bar that brilliant throw from Wareham - has not found its wares tonight. Full and outside off, Knight looks to drive but gets an outside edge to short third man. She comes halfway down for the single but is sent back. She is gone for all money when short third man returns a decent throw to Healy - but she lets it go, thinking it will hit the stumps and it doesn't! Why didn't she collect?
Full and outside off, blasted through the covers for a single.
A bit of sawdust being applied around the bowler's landing area. Meanwhile, Sophie Molineux returns. 1-0-12-0 so far.
Steers this through third man for a single.

DROPPED! Third drop of the match and all off Wyatt! She has definitely had King Midas give her some of his powers for this game. Another ordinary piece of fielding. Full on middle, Danielle hits it straight back but Kimmince is late to react. The ball hits her palms and lobs behind. She tries to  take it on the rebound but can't.
A full toss, pushed past the non-striker to long on for a single.
On middle and leg, worked straight to short mid-wicket this time.
Full and outside off, driven straight to Meg Lanning at short extra cover.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
A full toss on leg stump, watchfully defended. 10 runs from that over, but a wicket as well.
FOUR! What a shot again. Short and outside off, cut behind point for a boundary!
Outside off, guided past past first slip to third man for a single.
In comes the skipper, Heather Knight, at number 5, replacing Sciver.

OUT! Plumb LBW! England waste their review, just delaying Elysse Perry in getting her 100TH T20I WICKET! Full and straight, swinging in, Sciver walks a long way across and tries to flick but misses. Is hit on the pads and the umpire thinks for a while but then raises his finger! Natalie immediately goes for the review, without even consulting her partner. The third umpire checks for the inside edge but nothing comes up on the Snickometer. Hawk Eye shows it to be plumb and the decision stays as it is! Sciver is not happy. She believes she got some wood on that.
Review time! Sciver has been adjudged LBW but she has taken the review straightaway.
Yorker outside off, squeezed through point for a single.
FOUR! What a shot. Full and outside off, Wyatt jumps down the track and drives it between cover and mid off for a boundary!
A slower ball outside off, short in length, Natalie pulls but misses. 40/2 IN THE POWERPLAY - Decent for both sides. England starting well, Australia bouncing back.
Comes down the track this time and hits it through the covers for one.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a run.
WIDE. Second one of the over. This is down the leg side, Sciver misses her sweep.
Pushes this through mid off for a single.
WIDE. Miles outside off, left alone.
Comes down the track and swings hard but gets a bottom edge.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Delissa Kimmince to bowl now.
Full and outside off, steered to third man for a single. 10 runs but a wicket as well from the over.
Natalie Sciver comes in at number 4, replacing Jones.

OUT! Not even in the frame! The in-form batter has come and gone. Spectacular piece of fielding from Georgia Wareham. A length ball on middle, Jones whips this through mid-wicket and calls for a quick single. Wareham does not have to move much and hence has that extra second to take aim. But she has got only one stump to see. That is enough for her. Bull's eye! Jones dives but she fears for the worst. And replays shown why. Gone by 2 yards.
DIRECT HIT! Is Jones gone? Referred upstairs...
FOUR! CLUBBED! Not all that short from Perry but Jones rocks back and pulls it over square leg for a boundary!
Full ad straight, watchfully defended.
It comes back in, takes the inside edge, goes to the leg side and the batters take a quick single.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Australia looking ragged now. Landed outside off, Wyatt steers it through third man. It goes straight to Delissa Kimmince who takes it a bit easy bending low to her left but it goes through. Unusual start from Australia. Pretty nervous they look.
A stifled appeal for LBW, turned down. Full and swinging in, going down leg, Jones misses her flick and is hit on the pads.
Jumps out and steers it through point where a very good stop is made at short third man. A single taken.

LUCKY! Wyatt certainly has a lot of luck tonight. Outside off, Danielle looks to run it down to third man but the ball swings in, takes the inside edge and goes past the stumps to fine leg! Two runs taken.
Outside off, moving away, a play and a miss.
Amy Jones comes in at number 3, replacing Beaumont.

OUT! Caught! Australia catch this one. Ordinary cricket from Beaumont. No need to play this shot with Wyatt going so well at the other end. A length ball outside off, Tammy jumps down the track, looks to go big but is not quite to the pitch of the ball. No pace off the pitch and she plays early. Miscues the shot and gets a top edge high in the air. Simple catch for Elysse Villani at mid off.
Outside off, coming in sharply, played through point for a single.
Comes down the track and whips it over mid-wicket, just over the leaping fielder for a couple.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Outside off, Beaumont looks to run it down to third man but is beaten.
Outswinger, outside off, pushed towards point.

EDGED, BUT DROPPED! Ordinary effort from Alyssa Healy and Australia have not started this final well. This was a regulation catch. A short ball outside off, Wyatt jumps out, looks to slash but the ball moves away and takes the outside edge. It goes straight to Healy behind who perhaps is surprised by the carry. The previous ones did not come on so quickly. She fumbles and the ball goes off her right glove. A single to third man. Costly. Very costly.
Outside off, on a length, Wyatt pushes and misses.
A change already. Ellyse Perry into the attack early.
Outside off, seaming away, a play and a miss.
On a length outside off, watchfully defended.

IN THE AIR, DROPPED! Is that the luck England need? Though, a more logical statement would be - Haynes has saved a boundary. Short and outside off, Wyatt cuts hard and aerial through backward point. Rachael Haynes throws herself to her left but the ball bursts through her hand. Tough chance but these are crucial moments in such a big game. A single taken.
This one goes away. Danielle hangs her bat and misses again.
On a length outside off, moves in even more, Wyatt feels for it but misses.
On middle, cutting in sharply, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Megan Schut to bowl from the other end.
Outside off, punched straight to point. 12 runs from the opening over, great start from England.
A dot ball. Full and outside off, spinning away, Danielle looks to defend but the ball spins away, takes the outside edge and goes to short third man.
SIX! Ho ho ho! This is even better! England taking the attack to Australia pretty early. Floated once more, down the track comes Wyatt and lofts it over long off once again!
FOUR! 'That is the way to start a World Cup final!' remarks Mel Jones on air. Flighted outside off, Wyatt jumps out, gets to the pitch of the ball and lofts it over mid off for a boundary!
Outside off, pushed through the covers for a run. Both the openers are underway.
Off the mark straightaway. Short and outside off, Wyatt goes back and punches it through the covers for a single.
Right then. The anthems are done and dusted. Let us play. The English openers make their way out to the middle - Danielle Wyatt and Tammy Beaumont. Sophie Molineux to begin to Wyatt. Here we go...
Time for the national anthem. 'Long live the Queen!' first up, followed by 'Advance Australia Fair!'

Sir Curtly Ambrose walks out with the trophy with a big smile on his face. Which captain will be smiling at the end of the game, holding it? Then the sound of ICC events - that music which makes your hair stand - is being played. My colleague Akash, aka ABK, is a big fan of this music, raising the TV volume to a 100 whenever this gets played. However, now, he must be sleeping soundly.
TEAM NEWS - Not surprisingly, neither team has made any changes to its winning combination.

PITCH REPORT - Lisa Sthalekar observes that there is less grass cover and a nice sheen is visible on the track. Predicts that batting first is the best time to bat with the pitch expected to slow down.

Australian captain, Meg Lanning, is not too perturbed as she reckons that the wicket looks great and should stay the same throughout. Admits that Australia needed to play out of their skins in the semi-final and need to play extremely well here again. Hopes that Alyssa Healy has another great game but is also confident that if she misses out, someone or the other will step up.

England skipper, Heather Knight, says that the wicket looks much better and she wants to get some runs on the board and defend that. Is proud of the win in the semi-final with her side showing the intensity needed in a semi-final. Is confident of her batting unit but reckons that they need to play even better against Australia who have got a great bowling attack. On Alyssa Healy, Knight says that she has had a great World Cup but she is not the only threat as Australia have a great batting line-up. Says that this is a big game but wants her side to enjoy and do the basics right, reckoning that the rest will take care of itself.
TOSS - Time for the most important event of the game. Meg Lanning spins the coin, Heads, is the call from Heather Knight and Heads it is. ENGLAND WILL BAT.
WEATHER - We had some RAIN earlier but now it is pretty clear. No more of that, please!

Australia may have been dominant in 2018 but in this tournament, they have not been at their best. They finally got their 'A' game against the Windies in the semi-final and will aim to maintain that intensity. England on the other hand, have been like a dark horse. Not threatening at any stage but never one to be taken lightly. And here they are, a step away from their maiden WWT20 title, second WT20 trophy (men and women) and second consecutive ICC silverware. Let's hope for a cracker.

Ahoy Sunday! If you are in that part of the world where the sun is about to rise. Hello, Saturday night! If you are in the time zone of the place where this mega match is to be played. Australia vs England. The oldest and biggest rivalry ever. Gender does not matter. And in this case, the context matters even more. The game which both teams would have dreamt of playing. Only one can make that come true. Who will it be? Experienced Australia? Or enterprising England? Hello and a warm welcome to the final of the Women's World T20 in Antigua.
